newsitem.title: INDIA: India rulers see little hope for Congress truce.
newsitem.headline: India rulers see little hope for Congress truce.

text.p: India's ruling coalition said on Wednesday that make-or-break talks with rebellious Congress party to save Prime Minister H. D. Deve Gowda's ten-month-old government may not succeed.

"My prognosis is I don't think the talks will succeed, not in the second round, not in the third round," a senior alliance official told reporters after leaders adjourned for the night after a first round of formal talks.
"The 2 1/2-hour-long discussion today was mainly over the Congress delegates' demand for the coronation of Mr. Sitaram Kesri (Congress president) as prime minister," the official said.
"The United Front delegates summarily rejected the suggestion," the official said. "But both sides have agreed to resume their discussions tomorrow."
"The coalition's delegates offered to set up a mechanism to address the grievances of Congress party in the future," the official said.
Kesri withdrew Congress' support for Deve Gowda on March 30, citing the United Front's alleged failure to check communalism among other reasons.

The coalition's delegates were later locked in talks with Deve Gowda, apparently working out a strategy for a vote of confidence the prime minister faces in parliament on Friday, United Front officials said.
United Front spokesman Jaipal Reddy said the talks were held in a cordial atmosphere but gave no details.
The 11-day-old crisis has jolted the nation's financial markets.
Officially, both sides said they were satisified with Wednesday's talks.

"We will have further discussions. We will try to resolve the crisis," coalition leader Chandrababu Naidu said, adding that the talks, which he called cordial, were set to resume on Thursday at 9:30 a.m. (0400 GMT).

The prospect that both sides could resolve their differences ahead of Friday's vote drove the Bombay Stock Exchange's benchmark 30-share index up 131.80 points, or 3.74 percent, to end at a provisional close of 3,652.29.
The 15-member United Front has 180 deputies in the 545-seat lower house of parliament, the Lok Sabha, while the Congress has 140 lawmakers.
The right-wing Hindu Bharatiya Janata Party emerged as the single largest party from inconclusive elections in May last year. It controls 193 seats, including allies.
Earlier on Wednesday, members of both delegations were smiling and looked cheerful as they posed for photographers.
Deve Gowda said earlier on Wednesday he expected the crisis to ease before the vote on Friday.

"I do not want to predict what will be the outcome. But I hope there will be some positive solution to some of the issues," the Press Trust of India (PTI) news agency quoted him as saying ahead of the formal talks.
Deve Gowda said he hoped parliament would pass the 1997/98 (April-March) budget ahead of the confidence vote.
"I even now expect and I hope that all political parties will cooperate to pass the finance bill and the budget pending before parliament on April 11," Deve Gowda said.
The budget that proposed corporate and personal tax cuts welcomed by industry has been held hostage by the crisis.
